paths.description: Homepage and downloader entry, the primary public task and shared site template.
Primary URL-entry flow and invalid/empty submission entry state; a real third-party media download was intentionally not performed.
Arabic localized/RTL template representing the 26 alternate-language routes.

findings.summary: The page does not follow the system dark-color preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode probe matched prefers-color-scheme: dark, but html computed color-scheme remained normal and body stayed rgb(249, 250, 251).
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven dark surface and text tokens.

findings.summary: Consent content fails minimum contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found 1.82:1 contrast for “Learn more” and 2.8:1 for the partners link against the dimmed consent surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Raise foreground/background contrast to at least WCAG AA and verify forced-colors.

findings.summary: Route changes have no authored View Transition.
findings.evidence: Rendered CSS/DOM contained no view-transition declarations or startViewTransition usage across the home and FAQ routes.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a progressive cross-document View Transition for navigation, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: The long page offers little scroll-state guidance.
findings.evidence: The page is roughly 9,048 CSS px tall on mobile, but inspected CSS contains no scroll-state query, progress indicator, or shrinking-header behavior.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight scroll progress or scroll-state-aware header treatment for long pages.

findings.summary: A consent wall obscures the primary task on every fresh visit.
findings.evidence: Desktop and 360px screenshots show a modal consent prompt covering the downloader and most of the viewport before interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide an equally prominent reject option and keep core content visible and usable before a choice.
findings.guidanceId: avoid intrusive interstitial popup content first

findings.summary: The consent modal is an ad-hoc div rather than a dialog primitive.
findings.evidence: DOM inspection found visible DIV role=dialog overlays and no <dialog> or popover elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Use <dialog> for the modal flow with platform focus, escape, and dismissal behavior.

findings.summary: Repeated components do not use component-level responsiveness.
findings.evidence: The CSS probe found no @container usage even though feature/navigation components are reused across widths.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable components containment and adapt them with size container queries where layout changes.

findings.summary: The primary downloader is blocked by consent before users can act.
findings.evidence: Repeated fresh-session flow captures never exposed an immediate reject path; the modal covers the URL field and asks to share data with 210 partners.
findings.suggestedFix: Let users reach the downloader without accepting tracking, with reject and manage choices at the same level.

findings.summary: Main-thread blocking is above the good Lighthouse diagnostic range.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured 240 ms Total Blocking Time; the mobile layout observer also recorded a 72 ms long task.
findings.suggestedFix: Break up or defer non-critical JavaScript, especially advertising and consent work.

findings.summary: Third-party scripts dominate a relatively simple page load.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 1,128,147 transferred bytes; 625,217 bytes were third-party and 875,583 bytes were scripts.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer optional third parties until consent/intent and trim the critical dependency chain.

findings.summary: The page ships substantial unused JavaScript and CSS.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 440 KiB unused JavaScript and 30 KiB unused CSS; app.js was about 65% unused.
findings.suggestedFix: Split the app bundle by route/feature and load ad/CMP code only when required.

findings.summary: Transport policy and cookies lack baseline hardening.
findings.evidence: Headers found no CSP or HSTS; cookies found six without Secure, including analytics cookies using SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Set HSTS and a restrictive CSP, and mark all HTTPS cookies Secure with the narrowest SameSite policy.

findings.summary: The default tracking footprint is excessive.
findings.evidence: Tracker capture found 8 third-party origins and Google Analytics, Tag Manager, and AdSense; the consent UI names 210 partners.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimise vendors and defer analytics/advertising requests until a valid choice requires them.

findings.summary: Several browser-enforced defenses are missing.
findings.evidence: The main response omitted Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options, CSP, and HSTS; only X-Frame-Options was present.
findings.suggestedFix: Add nosniff, strict referrer and permissions policies, HSTS, and CSP frame-ancestors.

findings.summary: The app-like utility has no verified offline fallback.
findings.evidence: A manifest is linked, but the runtime probe found no active service-worker registration.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a minimal service worker and useful offline/error shell, or explicitly scope offline support out.
findings.guidanceId: offline fallback service worker web app manifest installable pwa

findings.summary: Consent choices are not presented symmetrically.
findings.evidence: The first prompt offers Consent and Manage options, but no direct Reject all action, while describing sharing with 210 partners.
findings.suggestedFix: Present Reject all beside Accept all with equal prominence and preserve the choice.

findings.summary: Images are not consistently responsive or modern.
findings.evidence: Image inspection found 12 images without srcset, 10 legacy-format assets, 7 below-fold images not lazy-loaded, and one oversized image.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve AVIF/WebP responsive sources and lazy-load non-critical images.

findings.summary: Advertising and analytics create avoidable background work.
findings.evidence: HAR showed 16 third-party requests and 625,217 third-party bytes, including analytics calls and large ad scripts on initial load.
findings.suggestedFix: Delay, batch, or remove background analytics and advertising work until it provides user value.

findings.summary: Third-party payload is disproportionate to the downloader UI.
findings.evidence: More than half of the 1.13 MB transfer was third-party; Tag Manager, AdSense, and the consent platform were among the largest resources.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party byte/request budget and load optional vendors only after consent and intent.

findings.summary: The initial memory footprint is heavy for a simple form/content page.
findings.evidence: The baseline heap summary contained 349,896 nodes and 20,714,412 self-size bytes before any download flow.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce ad/CMP and bundle allocations, then profile heap and DOM totals again.
findings.guidanceId: bounded memory footprint javascript heap size page weight proportionate allocations

taskList.title: Replace the tracking-first consent wall with symmetric Accept all / Reject all / Manage choices, and keep the downloader usable without tracking consent.
Harden response headers and cookies with CSP, HSTS, nosniff, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, Secure, and appropriate SameSite values.
Cut and defer ad, CMP, analytics, and unused application code to reduce blocking, transfer size, and background work.
Fix consent-dialog text and link contrast, including forced-colors behavior.
Add preference-driven dark mode with color-scheme and tested dark surface tokens.
Replace the ad-hoc consent overlay with a semantic dialog and platform focus/dismiss behavior.
Serve responsive modern images and lazy-load below-fold assets.
Reduce bundle/CMP allocations and repeat the heap comparison.
taskList.guidanceId: bounded memory footprint javascript heap size page weight proportionate allocations

taskList.title: Add a minimal service worker with an intentional offline/error shell.
taskList.guidanceId: offline fallback service worker web app manifest installable pwa

taskList.title: Progressively enhance navigation and long-page guidance with View Transitions and scroll-state feedback.
Adopt container queries for reusable feature and navigation components where their layout changes.
